transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a little trouble explaining myself clearly. It’s probably not as bad as I worry it is, but at work, someone will ask me something simple, like when a ring repair will be ready, and I’ll start answering and somehow I’m talking about invoices, then garden soil, then mortgage papers… and I can see their face sort of change, like I’ve lost them.

I don’t mean to do it. I know that sounds strange. I just… I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing I’m supposed to bring up here, but it’s been bothering me.
Do you feel anxious or upset when you realize you've lost track of what you're saying?

Yes… I do get a bit anxious, I guess. Mostly embarrassed. I’ll realize I started with, you know, a simple question about when a ring repair will be ready, and somehow I’ve wandered into invoices, then something about garden soil, or mortgage papers… and I can see the person kind of losing me.

I try to pull it back quickly, so it’s not like I’m trying to make a big scene or anything. It just makes me feel foolish, like I should be able to answer normally. Does that make sense?
Do you use alcohol or any other substances that might be affecting your thinking or speech?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not saying I’m perfect or anything, but I haven’t noticed alcohol or anything like that being connected to when I get muddled talking.

I’m not really sure what counts as “substances” in this context, though. Like, do you mean recreational drugs, or medications too? I don’t want to answer the wrong way.
Have you ever had a period where you felt detached from reality or had strange beliefs or perceptions?

I… maybe a little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

Sometimes at the showroom, I’ve gotten this feeling—well, more than a feeling at the time—that certain customers are coming in just to see if I’ll slip up or miss payments. Like they ask too many questions about the new showroom, and I start thinking they’re checking on us, not just being friendly.

My husband says they’re probably only making conversation, and I can sort of see that when he says it. But in the moment, it feels very real to me. Does that count as what you mean?
Do you still think those customers are checking on you when you're not feeling anxious or embarrassed about your speech?

I’d like to say no, because that would sound more sensible… but sometimes, yes. Even when I’m not especially anxious or embarrassed, I can still get convinced they’re sort of checking on me.

It’s usually when they ask a lot about the new showroom or seem too interested in how things are going. My husband will say, “They’re just being friendly,” and I can understand that after the fact, but in the moment it feels like they’re watching to see if I’ll miss payments or something.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m not trying to be difficult or paranoid—I just… that’s how it can feel to me.
Do you think those customers are checking on you most of the time, or is it just occasionally?

I wouldn’t say most of the time, no… at least I hope not. It’s more occasional.

But when it happens, I can get pretty convinced in the moment that some customers are coming in to check whether I’ll miss payments, especially if they keep asking questions about the new showroom. My husband tells me they’re probably just being friendly, and I do try to take that in… but sometimes it still feels like they’re checking on me. I know that sounds odd.
How long have you been having these feelings that certain customers are checking on you?

I think it started… around a year and eight months ago, maybe. Not every day or anything, but that’s about when I first noticed getting those worries that certain customers were watching us or checking on me.

I don’t know if I’m putting that the right way, but… yes, roughly that long.
Do you think those customers are actually checking on you even when your husband or others tell you they're just being friendly?

I know this may sound strange, and I’m not saying it happens all the time… but yes, sometimes I do still think they’re actually checking on me.

Even when my husband says they’re just being friendly, if they ask too many questions about the new showroom, I can get convinced they’re really there to see whether I’ll miss payments or something like that. I know that probably doesn’t sound very reasonable, but in the moment it feels real to me.
Do you ever have times where you completely don't think those customers are checking on you at all?

Yes… I mean, there are definitely times I don’t think that at all. Most customers I can see are probably just asking normal questions.

It’s more that certain ones, when they ask too much about the new showroom, I start feeling like they’re checking whether I’ll miss payments. Even after my husband says they’re only being friendly, sometimes I still get convinced. I know that sounds odd… but it’s not constant, if that makes sense.
Do you ever think that those customers who you believe are checking on you are part of a larger plot or conspiracy against you?

Not really a larger plot… at least, I don’t think of it that way. It’s more just certain customers.

I know it sounds odd, but when they ask a lot about the new showroom, I can get convinced they’re coming in to check whether I’ll miss payments or something. Even when my husband says they’re only being friendly, it can still feel like that to me. But I wouldn’t say it’s some big conspiracy… if that makes sense.
Do you think these beliefs about customers checking on you are something that you could be wrong about?

Yes… I mean, I can admit I could be wrong about it. I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

It’s just that in the moment, when certain customers ask too many questions about the new showroom, I get convinced they’re there to check whether I’ll miss payments. Even when my husband says they’re just being friendly, it can still feel true to me.

But sitting here talking to you, yes… I know there’s a chance I’m misreading it.
Do you think the belief that certain customers are checking on you is something that you've had consistently over the past year and eight months?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but that sounds about right.

The worries about certain customers checking on us started around a year and eight months ago. It hasn’t been every single minute or anything, but it’s been there off and on since then. Is that the kind of timeline you mean?
Have you ever believed that certain customers are checking on you for a reason that seems unusual or impossible to others?

Yes… I guess so. I mean, I know it probably sounds strange when I say it out loud.

It’s just that sometimes certain customers ask a lot of questions about the new showroom, and I get this feeling—more than a feeling, really—that they’re there to check whether I’m going to miss payments or something. My husband tells me they’re just being friendly, and I do try to take that in… but at the time it can still feel like they have a reason for asking.

I’m not saying it makes perfect sense. I just… that’s how it feels sometimes.
Have you ever believed that certain customers are checking on you for a reason that couldn't possibly be true?

I… I don’t know if I’d say “couldn’t possibly” be true, because I know that sounds extreme. But yes, there have been times I’ve gotten pretty convinced of it.

Like when certain customers come in and ask too many questions about the new showroom, I start thinking they’re really there to check whether we’ll miss payments. My husband says they’re just being friendly, and I try to believe him, but in the moment it feels like there’s a reason behind it.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything.
Do you think your beliefs about certain customers checking on you have changed at all over the past year and eight months?

I think they’ve… maybe gotten a little more fixed at times, if that’s the right way to say it. I try not to make too much of it, because I know it sounds odd, and my husband will say they’re only being friendly.

But when certain customers come in and ask a lot of questions about the new showroom, I can still get convinced they’re really checking whether I’m going to miss payments. It hasn’t turned into something different exactly, but I guess it’s been easier for me to believe it in the moment than I’d like to admit.
Have your beliefs about certain customers checking on you ever changed or been disproven in any way?

I guess… sometimes my husband saying they’re just being friendly makes me question it a little afterward. Like once I’m calmer, I can see that maybe I read too much into it.

But in the moment, when they’re asking a lot about the new showroom, it still feels like they’re checking on whether I’m going to miss payments. I know that sounds odd, and I’m not saying I have proof exactly… it just hasn’t fully gone away, if that makes sense.
Have you ever believed that certain customers are checking on you for a reason that is completely implausible or impossible?

Completely impossible… I don’t know. I don’t want to overstate it. I know it probably sounds odd, and maybe that’s what you mean.

But yes, I’ve gotten convinced some customers are coming in just to check whether I’ll miss payments, especially when they ask too many questions about the new showroom. Even when my husband says they’re only being friendly, I still sometimes feel like there’s another reason they’re there.

I know I may be reading into it too much. I’m trying to be honest without making it sound worse than it is.
Have you ever believed that certain customers are checking on you for a reason that is not only impossible but also completely bizarre or unbelievable to others?

I wouldn’t say… bizarre exactly. I mean, I hope not. I know it may sound odd to other people, and I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is.

It’s more that I’ve gotten convinced certain customers are coming in to check whether I’m going to miss payments, because they ask too many questions about the new showroom. Even after my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, I can still feel like there’s something behind it.

But completely unbelievable… I don’t know. Maybe to someone else it would sound that way.
Do you think your belief that certain customers are checking on you is based on reality or is it something that might not be true at all?

I think… part of me feels like it’s based on something real, because they do ask a lot of questions about the new showroom. So in the moment it really seems like they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments.

But I also know my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, and when I’m calmer I can see that maybe I don’t actually know that’s why they’re there. So… it might not be true. I’m trying not to make too much of it, but it does feel real to me when it’s happening.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about customers checking on you is not based on any real evidence?

Yes… I think it’s possible. I don’t really have proof, not exactly. It’s just that when they ask a lot about the new showroom, my mind goes there and I get convinced they’re checking whether I’ll miss payments.

I know my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m accusing people for no reason. But in the moment it feels like evidence, even if later I can see it might not really be.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the nature and bizarreness of the patient's belief that customers are checking on her, which directly concerns delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
I wouldn’t say… bizarre exactly. I mean, I hope not. I know it may sound odd to other people, and I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is.

It’s more that I’ve gotten convinced certain customers are coming in to check whether I’m going to miss payments, because they ask too many questions about the new showroom. Even after my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, I can still feel like there’s something behind it.

But completely unbelievable… I don’t know. Maybe to someone else it would sound that way.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs about customers checking on them are delusional
doctor.question: Do you think your belief that certain customers are checking on you is based on reality or is it something that might not be true at all?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds odd, but I’ve gotten convinced some customers are coming in just to check whether I’ll miss payments, because they ask too many questions about the new showroom even after my husband says they’re only being friendly.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about whether the belief that customers are checking on me is reality-based or possibly untrue, which assesses the fixed persecutory-type belief described under delusions.

patient.answer:
I think… part of me feels like it’s based on something real, because they do ask a lot of questions about the new showroom. So in the moment it really seems like they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments.

But I also know my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, and when I’m calmer I can see that maybe I don’t actually know that’s why they’re there. So… it might not be true. I’m trying not to make too much of it, but it does feel real to me when it’s happening.

doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that your belief about customers checking on you is not based on any real evidence?

patient.answer:
Yes… I think it’s possible. I don’t really have proof, not exactly. It’s just that when they ask a lot about the new showroom, my mind goes there and I get convinced they’re checking whether I’ll miss payments.

I know my husband says they’re probably just being friendly, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m accusing people for no reason. But in the moment it feels like evidence, even if later I can see it might not really be.
